newsitem.title: USA: FBI exploring link with Atlanta, Washington bombs.
newsitem.headline: FBI exploring link with Atlanta, Washington bombs.

text.p: The FBI said on Tuesday it was investigating a possible link between last summer's bombing at the Atlanta Olympics and another bombing in Washington state.

"I cannot comment on any possible connection between the Atlanta bombing and suspects charged in another bombing case in the state of Washington, except to confirm that it is being thoroughly explored along with every other possibility," FBI Deputy Director Weldon Kennedy said in a statement.
"Every possibility in the Centennial Park bombing investigation is being taken very seriously. We literally have thousands of leads being pursued," Kennedy added.
Two people were killed and 111 injured in the July 27 bombing during last summer's Olympic games. The bomb went off in Centennial Park.

Three men from the Sandpoint, Idaho, area, Robert Berry, 42, Charles Barbee, 42, and Verne Merrell, 51, were arrested on Oct. 8 and charged with a pair of pipe bomb attacks and bank robberies last year outside Spokane. They are to stand trial next month in federal court on charges of bank robbery, weapons possession and conspiracy.
The Spokane Spokesman-Review said on Tuesday an Atlanta architect called the newspaper after a report that the men had emerged as possible suspects in the Olympic bombing.

The architect, who asked to remain anonymous, said he had provided the FBI earlier with a sketch of a man wearing a backpack he and his daughter saw in the park about an hour before the early-morning blast.
After seeing television reports about the suspects in Spokane, the architect said he was convinced that the man he saw was Berry.
"After seeing the pictures on TV today, I'm 100 percent sure that was him, Mr. Berry," he told the Spokesman-Review.
The architect's 25-year-old daughter told the newspaper she recalled seeing a "weird-looking man" as she and her family left the park about an hour before the bombing.
"I remember him well, because he kind of looked out of place," she told the newspaper. "He was walking as if he was intoxicated or stoned, staring at people."
Berry's lawyer, John Rogers, declined to comment and said the report came as a "bolt out of the blue" to him.
Barbee's lawyer, Roger Peven, categorically denied his client had any involvement in the Atlanta bombing.
"Mr. Barbee had nothing to do with the Atlanta case," Peven said.
The FBI planned to interview the architect and his daughter on Tuesday, the newspaper said.
Richard Jewell, a security guard at the park, was initially identified as the chief suspect in the Atlanta bombing, but was cleared of any involvement in October.
